title: Toronto groups demand justice after Black trans woman dies in police custody
article: Two Toronto advocacy groups say they're "shocked and outraged" and are calling for justice after a Black trans woman died while in police custody.

In a statement, which was released on social media Thursday, Nov. 5, Black Lives Matter - Toronto (BLMTO) and Maggie's Toronto Sex Workers Action Project identified the woman from Scarborough, who died in hospital on Oct. 26, as Coco. Her last name is not being revealed for "family privacy" reasons.
Both groups said the mystery surrounding Coco's death as well as her continued misgendering in Toronto police reports is "unacceptable".
"Black trans lives matter. Coco should be alive today. Toronto Police Services is responsible for her death in their custody," they charged.

BLMTO and Maggie's, which is one of Canada's oldest sex worker organizations serving Toronto's downtown east end for close to 40 years, went on to say Coco's death is an example of a corrupt system they say continually harms Black and trans people. They're calling for their voices and lives to be respected.
"We say no more, and never again! ... In order to have thriving communities supported by trans leadership, we need trans people to get to live long enough to become elders," they said.
"We deserve to live. Coco deserved to live!"
Further, they said Black trans people face "disproportionate targeting by the police and are often harassed and picked up by police simply for being trans in public space."

"Trans lives are inherently valuable and we demand an end to this over-policing of our community," they wrote, adding during a year when talk of defunding the police is top of mind, people in their communities are "repeatedly confronted by police violence and brutality."

"There have been far too many people killed this year alone in police custody or by the hands of police in this north part of Turtle Island and Inuit Nunangat. We are tired. We are frustrated. And we are activated."

Earlier this week, The 519, a City of Toronto agency and charitable non-profit in the Church-Wellesley area, along with the communities it serves, launched the #TPSWhatHappened? campaign to demand more information as well as accountability and transparency from Toronto police and Ontario's Special Investigations Unit (SIU), which is currently probing this incident.
The organization also wants to know why the SIU incorrectly shared the gender of their "much loved" community member, despite "being informed of this error".

Toronto Centre Coun. Kristyn Wong-Tam also issued a statement echoing their demands. She's also urging people to share their thoughts on Toronto police's Community Crisis Response Program by filling out an online survey .

Back on Oct. 26, the SIU identified the victim as a male. Late Wednesday afternoon, the civilian agency issued a follow-up news release in which the person who died was correctly identified as a trans woman.

Anyone concerned about this case is being urged to contact both 43 Division at 416-808-4300 and ask about case number 2020-2029228, and the SIU at 416-622-0748 and inquire about case number 20-TCD-284.

Further, anyone with information about this investigation is being asked to contact the lead SIU investigator at 1-800-787-8529 . Anyone with any video evidence related to this incident can upload that video through the SIU website.
